key_insight: The paper reframes token-budget selection for LLM reasoning as a risk-control problem and uses conformal-style calibration to set adaptive stopping thresholds that guarantee a user-specified error rate while reducing wasted computation.
problem_solved: How to decide when to keep spending tokens on multi-step LLM reasoning versus stopping early—balancing reliability (error rate) against compute—without relying on brittle heuristics and while providing statistical guarantees.
method: Calibrate per-step or per-instance stopping criteria on a validation set using conformal/statistical techniques to map model scores to error-risk estimates.
Formulate an optimization: for a target risk level (alpha), choose stopping thresholds that minimize expected token usage subject to the risk constraint.
Deploy adaptive inference: apply the learned stopping rule at test time to stop reasoning early when additional tokens are unlikely to reduce risk, providing dataset-level guarantees.
impact: Enables practitioners to trade compute for reliability with provable error control, improving efficiency of LLM reasoning deployments and making token-budgeting decisions principled and actionable.
visual_elements: Risk vs. Tokens curve: plot showing error rate as a function of token budget with a highlighted threshold that meets the target risk.
Adaptive reasoning flowchart: model generates steps → evaluate stopping score → continue or stop (with statistical guarantee badge).
Calibration plot: validation scores mapped to empirical error coverage used to choose conformal thresholds.
Bar chart/comparison: average tokens and error rate for fixed-budget baselines vs. the proposed adaptive, risk-controlled method.
paper_title: Conformal Thinking: Risk Control for Reasoning on a Compute Budget
paper_authors: Xi Wang, Anushri Suresh, Alvin Zhang, Rishi More, William Jurayj
